blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Despite advancements in automatic speech recognition systems (ASR), current systems exhibit speaker-attribute bias, i.e., their speech recognition performance is biased against certain speakers based on their demographic attributes such as gender, accents, and speaker type. However, accurately assessing speaker attribute bias in a given ASR system requires the availability of a bias evaluation dataset with comparable speech across subgroups of a speaker attribute. In this paper, we introduce African speech Bias Evaluation Dataset (AfriBED), a novel speech recognition bias evaluation dataset for two low resource African languages, Bemba and Nyanja, to detect and estimate gender and speaker-type bias for ASR systems. The dataset comprises 9 hours of speech with 3928 utterances recorded by 80 speakers for Bemba, while the Nyanja set includes 6260 utterances with approximately 18 hours of speech recorded by 127 speakers. The results of our baseline experiments demonstrate that the datasets are useful for examining gender and speaker-type attribute bias in the target languages.
blocks.zh: 尽管在自动语音识别系统(ASR)方面有所进步,但现行系统显示的语音属性偏差,即其语音识别表现基于性别、口音和语音类型等人口特征而偏向于某些语音。 然而,要准确评估某一ASR系统中的发言者属性偏差,就必须提供一套带有发言者属性各分组可比语音的偏向评价数据集。 在本文中,我们介绍了非洲语音比亚斯评价数据集(AfriBED),这是一个针对Bemba和Nyanja两种非洲低资源语言的新型语音识别偏差评价数据集,用于发现和估计ASR系统的性别和语音类型偏差。 数据集包括9小时的演讲和80名发言者为本巴录制的3928个发言,而Nyanja数据集包括6 260个发言,127名发言者录制了约18小时的发言。 我们的基线试验结果表明,数据集有助于审查目标语言中的性别和语种属性偏差。

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in developing ASR systems for low resource African languages [ 1 ] . With the majority of languages spoken across the continent classified as low resource languages (LRLs), most research efforts have focused on building training data dataset in order to improve ASR accuracy [ 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 ] . Although this research address the inherent limitations that characterize LRLs, one research dimension that has not received significant attention is how to effectively evaluate speech recognition models for speaker attribute biases [ 6 ] .
blocks.zh: 近年来,人们越来越有兴趣为非洲低资源语言开发ASR系统。 由于非洲大陆大多数语言被归类为低资源语言,大多数研究工作都侧重于建立培训数据集,以提高ASR的准确性[2、3、4、5]。 尽管这一研究涉及LRLs的内在局限性,但一个未引起极大关注的研究层面是如何有效评价演讲者属性偏差的语音识别模型[6].

blocks.en: In this paper, we present our data collection effort to address the issue of limited speech recognition bias evaluation datasets for African languages [ 7 , 8 ] . We introduce a novel bias evaluation dataset containing read speech in two low resource African languages: Bemba and Nyanja. The dataset is created for evaluating ASR systems for gender and speaker-type (native and non-native speaker) biases. We carefully constructed the datasets to ensure that the subgroups for each gender and speaker-type attribute have the same speech content to allow fair performance comparison. This is achieved by recording the same read text sentences by speakers of each speaker attribute subtype. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first to create dedicated ASR bias evaluation datasets to examine speaker-attribute bias in ASR systems for Bemba and Nyanja.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们介绍了我们为解决非洲语言有限语音识别偏差评价数据集问题而开展的数据收集工作[7、8]。 我们引入了一套新的偏见评价数据集,其中包含两种低资源非洲语言的读取语句:本巴语和尼亚尼亚语. 建立数据集是为了评估关于性别和演讲者(母语和非母语演讲者)偏见的ASR系统。 我们仔细设计了数据集,以确保每个性别和演讲者类型的属性的分组具有相同的演讲内容,以便能够进行公平的绩效比较。 这是通过记录每个发言者属性子类型的发言者读取的相同文字句子来实现的。 就我们所知,我们的工作是首先建立专门的ASR偏差评价数据集,以审查Bemba和NyanjaASR系统中的发言人偏差。

blocks.en: II Related work
blocks.zh: 二. 有关工作

blocks.en: Several bias evaluation datasets exist to evaluate ASR systems for various forms of speaker-attribute bias [ 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] . The most popular is the Artie Bias Corpus [ 10 ] based on the Mozilla Common Voice corpus [ 14 ] for age, gender, and accent bias detection. Liu et al. [ 12 ] created the Casual Conversations dataset for gender, age, and skin tone. Shriberg et al. [ 15 ] curated 72 hours of conversation-like speech based on dialogues from naturally-occuring meetings. There are others like the recently introduced FairSpeech [ 11 ] dataset. However, the majority of these datasets are designed for English ASR systems, leaving the majority of languages without tools to examine speaker attribute bias, particularly LRLs. In addition, the speech across attribute subgroups in these datasets is not the same. The subgroups of attributes do not have speech drawn from the same text sentences, resulting in unfair comparisons. In contrast, our study aims to create bias evaluation datasets for LRLs, targeting African languages. Therefore, we create a novel speech recognition bias evaluation dataset that covers two Sub-Saharan African languages: Bemba and Nyanja, which are spoken predominantly and widely in Zambia and neighboring countries [ 16 ] .
blocks.zh: 存在若干偏差评价数据集,用于评价各种形式的语音属性偏差的ASR系统[9、10、11、12、13]。 最受欢迎的是基于"Mozilla Couble Voice"的"Artie Bias Corpus [10]",用于年龄,性别和口音偏差的检测. 刘等. [12] 创建了Casual Conversations的性别,年龄,和皮肤语调数据集. 施里贝格等. [15] 整理了72小时的谈话类演讲,这些演讲以自然而然的会面的对话为基础。 还有一些类似最近推出的FairSpeech[11]数据集. 然而,这些数据集大多是为英语ASR系统而设计的,使得大多数语言没有工具来检查扬声器属性偏差,尤其是LRLs. 此外,这些数据集中跨属性子群的语音也不同. 属性分组没有从同一种文字句子中抽取出语音,导致不公平的比较. 相比之下,我们的研究旨在为LRLs创建偏差评价数据集,以非洲语言为对象. 因此,我们建立了一个新的语音识别偏差评价数据集,涵盖两种撒哈拉以南非洲语言:本巴语和尼扬贾语,赞比亚和邻国主要广泛使用这两种语言。

blocks.en: III Methodology
blocks.zh: 页:1 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we provide details of the different phases of our data collection process. We highlight that we obtained ethical clearance for data collection and followed all ethical standards for responsible data collection practices.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们详细介绍了我们数据收集过程的不同阶段。 我们强调,我们在数据收集方面获得了道德审查,并遵循了负责任的数据收集做法的所有道德标准。

blocks.en: III-A Demographic survey
blocks.zh: 三-A 人口调查

blocks.en:
We started by conducting a demographic survey among students at the University of Zambia, targeting students in the Department of Computing and Informatics using convenient sampling for our selection criteria. The survey was carried out for three reasons: to determine the native languages (amongst languages spoken in Zambia) spoken among the students who are our target population; to estimate the number of students we could invite to participate voluntarily in the successive phases; and to establish the demographic information that we could consider for our bias evaluation dataset.
The demographic survey was set up using the Google Forms platform and sent out to the students’ university email addresses.
blocks.zh:
我们首先对赞比亚大学学生进行人口调查,以计算和信息学系学生为对象,利用方便的抽样来制定我们的甄选标准。 调查有三个原因:确定作为我们目标人口的学生所讲的当地语言(赞比亚通用的语言);估计我们可邀请自愿参与各阶段的学生人数;建立人口信息,我们可以考虑我们的偏见评估数据集。
使用Google Forms平台进行人口调查,

blocks.en:
A total of 359 students responded to the survey. The responses showed that Bemba (41.23%) and Nyanja (44.57%) were the most populous native languages spoken among students and spoken as their first or second language. None of the other languages spoken had a critical mass.
Gender and speaker-type i.e., native and non-native speakers, were the two possible speaker attributes that could be captured for our data collection. 2 2 2 We define the first language as the native language the speaker has been exposed to since birth. A native speaker is one where the language is their first language, while a non-native speaker is one where the language is not their first language but they declare a good degree of proficiency in reading, understanding and writing. We did not find sufficiently large subgroups for other attributes such as race, age and region. All participants identified themselves as black, belonging to a single age group, between 18 and 25 years, and the majority (more than 70%) came from one region, Lusaka.
blocks.zh:
共有359名学生对调查作出答复。 答复表明,本巴语(41.23%)和尼扬贾语(44.57%)是学生中使用人口最多的母语,作为第一或第二语言。 其他语言中没有任何一种语言具有临界质量。
性别和演讲者类型,即本地和非本地演讲者,是可用于我们数据收集的两个演讲者属性。 2 2 我们把第一种语言定义为发言者自出生以来接触的母语。 母语是他们的第一语言,而非母语是他们的第一语言,但他们宣布在阅读、理解和写作方面有相当的熟练程度。 我们没有找到足够大的种族、年龄和区域等其他属性的分组。 所有参与者都确认自己是黑人,属于单一年龄组,年龄在18至25岁之间,大多数(70%以上)来自卢萨卡一个地区。

blocks.en: III-B Generating text sentences
blocks.zh: 三-B 生成文本句

blocks.en: Due to the lack of high-quality public textual data in our target languages, we obtained 1000 English text sentences from the test split of the open-source ASR dataset, LibriSpeech [ 17 ] and translated them into Bemba and Nyanja for audio recording. The LibriSpeech dataset comprises 1000 hours of speech in the English language derived from publicly domain audio books from the LibriVox project. 3 3 3 https://librivox.org/ To ensure that we obtained high-quality text translations, we recruited two paid professional translators, one translator per language, to translate the English sentences into the target languages. In addition, for each language, we recruited three native speakers (students) on a voluntary basis to verify and ensure that no mismatch occurred in the English-to-translation sentence pairs.
blocks.zh: 由于缺乏我们目标语言的高质量公共文本数据,我们从开源ASR数据集LibriSpeech [17]的测试分出1000个英文文本句子,并被翻译成了Bemba和Nyanja来录音. LibriSpeech数据集包含来自LibriVox项目的公有领域音频书所衍生的10小时英语语音. 3 3 3 https://librivox.org/ 为了确保我们获得高质量的文本翻译,我们征聘了两名付薪的专业翻译,每个语言一名翻译,将英文句子翻译成目标语言。 此外,对于每种语言,我们自愿招募了3名讲母语的人(学生),以核实并确保在英语到翻译的句子中不会出现不匹配的情况。

blocks.en: III-C Creating audio recordings
blocks.zh: 制作录音

blocks.en: We recruited a total of 205 students to record speech from translated text sentences on a voluntary basis. Most of the students were drawn from the participants in the survey who expressed interest in participating in the audio recording task. We carefully designed our recording strategy so that the speech between subgroups of the speaker attributes (gender and speaker type) is the same to ensure subgroup comparability. To achieve this, we defined two sets of speaker attribute groups: primary groups ( native male , non-native male , native female , and non-native female ) and secondary groups ( male , female , native and non-native ). The primary groups are intersectional attribute groups between gender and speaker-type attribute groups, while secondary groups are direct subgroups of gender (male and female) and speaker-type (native and non-native) attributes, whose data composition can be worked out and aggregated from the corresponding primary groups. To assign text sentences for audio recording to participants, we grouped the participants according to their self-identified primary groups. We then split the 1000 text sentences into two batches: Batch A , containing sentences 1–500, and Batch B , containing sentences 501–1000, and assigned them for recording to each primary group as shown in Fig. 1 . Furthermore, we split the text sentences in each batch into portions of 50 text sentences, which we then assigned to each participant to record. To ensure speech variation and diversity, and to allow in-group inter-speaker evaluation, we assigned each 50 sentence block to at least three participants. Using this strategy, gender and speaker-type subgroups can be assigned from the primary groups with speech in the subgroups based on the same sentences and without speaker overlap. The audio files were recorded using the Audacity software, with a sampling rate of 16kHz and 32-bit float PCM sample encoding setting. 4 4 4 https://www.audacityteam.org/ All the utterances are within 20 seconds.
blocks.zh: 我们共招募了205名学生,在自愿的基础上记录翻译文本句子的语音. 大多数学生来自调查参与者,他们表示有兴趣参与录音工作。 我们精心设计了录音战略,使发言者属性(性别和发言者类型)的分组之间的发言相同,以确保分组的可比性。 为此,我们界定了两组发言属性群体:主要群体(本地男性、非本地男性、本地女性和非本地女性)和第二群体(男性、女性、本地和非本地人)。 初级群体是性别与演讲者类属性群体之间的交叉属性群体,而次级群体是性别(男性和女性)和演讲者类属性(本土和非本土)的直接分组,其数据构成可以从相应的初级群体中确定和汇总. 为了向与会者分配录音的文字句子,我们按他们自己确定的主要群体对与会者进行了分组。 然后我们把1000个文字句子分成两批: 包含第1-500句的批A和包含第501-1000句的批B,并按图1所示将其分配给每个主组进行录音. 此外,我们将每批中的案文句子分成50个案文句子的部分,然后分配给每个参与者记录。 为了确保语音的变异和多样性,并允许小组间语言员的评价,我们把每50个句子块分配给至少3名参加者。 利用这一战略,可以从主要小组中指派性别和演讲者类型的分组,在分组中发表基于相同句子的演讲,而不出现演讲者重叠。 音频文件使用Audacity软件录制,取样率为16克 Hz和32位浮标PCM样本编码设置. 4 4 4 https://www.audacityteam.org/ 所有言论都在20秒之内。

blocks.en: Figure 1: Our strategy for allocating text sentences to primary subgroups to create audio recordings, ensuring comparable speech between subgroups of both gender and speaker-type attributes and without speaker overlap.
blocks.zh: 图1:我们把文字句子分配给主要分组以制作录音,确保性别和演讲者类特征分组之间可比较的发言,并且不出现演讲者重叠的战略。

blocks.en: Table I: Summary statistics of the bias evaluation datasets with Native Male (NM), Native female (NF), non-native male (NNM) and non-native female (NNF) primary intersectional speaker attribute subgroups.
blocks.zh: 表一:与原生男性(NM),原生女性(NF),非原生男性(NNM)和非原生女性(NNF)主要相交语属性分组的偏差评价数据集汇总统计.

blocks.en: Table II: Results of fine-tuned ASR models evaluated on overall sets of the language datasets. We report CER on the following subgroups: native male (N), non-native male (NNM), native female (NF), non-native female (NNF), male (M), Female (F), native (N), non-native (NN) and combined (C). Results are averaged over three runs. Lower CER and CER-gap values are better. We report mean and standard deviation (in parentheses) values.
blocks.zh: 表二:在语言数据集总体数据集上评价的微调ASR模型的结果. 我们报告以下分组的CER:本地男性(N)、非本地男性(NNM)、本地女性(NF)、非本地女性(NNF)、男性(M)、女性(F)、本地(NN)、非本地(NN)和合并(C)。 结果平均分为三轮。 较低的CER和CER-gap值较好. 我们报告平均值和标准差值(括号内)。

blocks.en: III-D Data validation
blocks.zh: 三-D 数据验证

blocks.en: We validated all data collected following the strategy of Conneau et al. [ 18 ] to ensure that only clean and high quality audio recordings were retained. All valid recordings, from either quiet or noisy environments, are kept as is.
blocks.zh: 我们验证了按照Conneau等人的战略收集的所有数据,以确保只保留干净和高质量的录音。 所有有效的录音,无论是安静的还是吵闹的环境,都保持原样。

blocks.en: III-E Resulting Datasets
blocks.zh: 三-E 结果数据集

blocks.en: Table I provides summary counts of audio files, number of speakers, and size (in hours) for each subgroup in the resulting evaluation sets. The overall datasets comprise a total of 9.32 hours of Bemba speech (3,928 audio files from 80 speakers) and 18.53 hours of Nyanja speech (6,260 audio files from 127 speakers). In addition, we curated subsets of the overall datasets into mini-version datasets, which include only speech recordings for text segments with at least one contribution from each subgroup, ensuring balanced and comparable evaluation across subgroups. The mini-version datasets include 3.13 hours of Bemba speech (1,396 files from 28 speakers) and 3.57 hours of Nyanja speech (1,198 files from 24 speakers). The dataset, along with transcriptions and anonymized metadata files, are released publicly to the research community under a Creative Commons BY-NC license. 5 5 5 The dataset is publicly available at: https://github.com/csikasote/AfriBED
blocks.zh: 表一列出各分组在评价组中的音频文件、发言者人数和大小(小时)的汇总数字。 总体数据集包括9.32小时的本巴演讲(80名发言者的3 928个音频文件)和18.53小时的尼亚尼亚演讲(127名发言者的6 260个音频文件)。 此外,我们把总体数据集的子集整理成小型版数据集,其中只收录每个分组至少提供一份稿件的文字部分的语音录音,确保各分组的评价均衡而可比较。 小型版数据集包括3.13小时的本巴演讲(1 396个文件来自28名发言者)和3.57小时的尼亚尼亚演讲(1 198个文件来自24名发言者)。 数据集,连同笔录和匿名元数据文件,根据创用CC BY-NC许可向研究界公开发布. 5 数据集可在https://github.com/csikasote/AfriBED上公开查阅。

blocks.en: IV Baseline Experiments
blocks.zh: 四. 基线实验

blocks.en:
To provide baseline speech recogntion and fairness performances of speech models in the target languages, we fine-tune two popular open-source pre-trained speech models: massively multilingual model for speech (MMS) [ 19 ] and the Africa-centric self-supervised multilingual speech model for Sub-Sahara African languages (SSA-HuBERT-Large-60K) [ 20 ] on existing open-source labeled ASR datasets for Bemba (28 hours) and Nyanja (25 hours) from Zambezi Voice [ 3 ] . The datasets are not balanced with speaker-type and gender attribute speech. We use the 300M and 1B parameter variants of both models.
We report character error rate (CER) metric [ 21 ] for ASR performance. For bias, we use the absolute difference in ASR performance between the subgroups of the respective speaker attributes (CER-gap) [ 22 ] .
We use our full collected dataset to evaluate the fine-tuned speech models.
blocks.zh:
为了提供目标语言语音模型的基线语音回溯和公平表现,我们微调了两种流行的开源前训练的语音模型:大规模多语种语音模型(MMS)[19]和以非洲为中心的分撒哈拉非洲语言的自控多语种语音模型(SSA-HuBERT-Large-60K)[20],现有开源软件标注的Bemba(28小时)和Nyanja(25小时)来自Zambezi Voice[3]. 数据集与演说者类型和性别属性的言论不相平衡. 我们使用两个模型的300M和1B参数变体.
我们报告ASR性能的字符出错率(CER)度量 [21]. 对于偏差,我们使用相应扬声器属性(CER-gap)的分组之间ASR性能的绝对差异[22].
我们利用我们收集的完整数据集来评估精细的语音模型.

blocks.en: V Results
blocks.zh: 五 结果

blocks.en: Table II provides the results of our baseline experiments. Below we provide key observations, and also compare to the findings of Sikasote et al. [ 6 ] , who evaluated gender bias for Bemba and Nyanja ASR on test sets without overlapping sentences between the male and female speech.
blocks.zh: 表二提供了我们基线试验的结果。 下面我们提供关键的意见,并与Sikasote等人的调查结果进行比较。 [6],他评价了Bemba和Nyanja ASR在测试集上的性别偏见,没有男女演讲的重复句子.

blocks.en: V-A Bias Analysis for Bemba
blocks.zh: Bemba的Bias分析

blocks.en: We observe performance disparities across all speaker attribute categories for all fine-tuned models. All models perform better in recognizing speech for native than non-native speakers, suggesting potential bias against non-native speakers in the models. All models perform better in recognizing male than female speech with relatively low CER-gap compared to other attributes. In contrast, Sikasote et al. [ 6 ] found inconsistent bias patterns between two evaluation sets both without sentence overlap between the subgroups.
blocks.zh: 我们看到,所有经过微调的模型,所有发言者属性类别的业绩差异。 所有模式在承认母语者的发言方面表现优于非母语者,表明模式中可能偏向非母语者。 与其他属性相比,所有模型都较好地识别了CER-gap相对较低的男性语音. 相形之下,Sikasote et al. [6] 发现两个评价组之间的偏差模式不一致,两个分组之间没有句子重叠。

blocks.en: V-B Bias Analysis for Nyanja
blocks.zh: Nyanja的V-B偏见分析

blocks.en: We observe significantly higher CER and CER-gap values in Nyanja than in Bemba. We attribute this to the possible impact of background noise. Our speech analysis revealed that approximately 1.5 hours of the total Nyanja data is non-speech compared to Bemba, with only 45 minutes. Similarly to Bemba for the Speaker Type attribute, all models perform better in recognizing speech for native speakers than non-native speakers, suggesting potential bias against non-native speakers in the models. For gender, all fine-tuned models exhibit bias against male speakers, consistent with the pattern observed in the study by Sikasote et al. [ 6 ] .
blocks.zh: 我们看到Nyanja的CER和CER-gap值明显高于Bemba。 我们将此归因于背景噪音的可能影响。 我们的言论分析显示,与本巴相比,Nyanja的全部数据中大约1.5小时是非言论的,只有45分钟。 与 " 议长类型 " 属性的Bemba类似,所有模式都比非母语的发言者更好地承认本地发言者的发言,这表明模式中可能存在对非母语发言者的偏见。 就性别而言,所有经过微调的模型都表现出对男性演讲者的偏见,这与Sikasote等人在研究中观察到的模式是一致的。 [6].

blocks.en: VI Conclusion
blocks.zh: 六. 结论

blocks.en: This paper introduces AfriBED, a bias evaluation dataset created to examine gender and speaker-type bias in ASR systems for two low resource African languages: Bemba and Nyanja. The dataset’s key innovation is that the subgroups of each speaker attribute have the same speech content, making the subgroups comparable for bias evaluation. The results of our baseline experiments demonstrate the usefulness of our datasets to examine gender and speaker-type attribute bias in ASR models for Bemba and Nyanja. In the future, we plan to expand our dataset to more languages, and to add additional speaker attributes.
blocks.zh: 本文介绍了AfriBED,这是一个偏向性评价数据集,用于审查非洲两种低资源语言(Bemba和Nyanja)在ASR系统中的性别和语种偏见。 数据集的关键创新是,每个发言人属性的分组具有相同的语音内容,使得分组可以比较偏见评价. 我们的基线试验结果表明,我们的数据集对审查本巴和尼扬贾的ASR模型中的性别和语音类型属性偏差很有用。 今后,我们计划将我们的数据集扩展到更多的语言,并增加额外的扬声器属性.
